title: Light, regular letter forms
focus: Notice the light line, clear lower turns, and common letter height. Keep your own dated starting sample before you copy the models.

title: Test the point and paper
focus: Use light straight and curved trial strokes to check that your point moves smoothly and your paper keeps a clean edge. Shading is not needed for this first tool test.

title: Supported writing position
focus: Observe the supported forearm, stable feet, and other hand holding the sheet. Adjust your own desk and page for relaxed movement rather than copying the furniture height.

title: A light, supported grip
transcription: Two views of the pen hold
focus: See how the thumb and fingers support the holder while the hand rests lightly on the page. These are historical views of the grip, not a left-handed setup diagram.

title: The same slant for either hand
focus: Keep the same right-leaning letter axis when writing with the left hand. Change page position for comfort; do not mirror the letter forms.

title: The main 52° slant
focus: Read the angle upward from the horizontal baseline to the right-leaning stem. This is the letter axis, not the angle of the page on your desk.

title: Height and width units
focus: The undotted i supplies one height unit; the space between the two stems of u supplies one width unit in the Key. Use these units to compare proportions while allowing the connecting curves to stay shallower than the main stems.

title: Compare curves and turns
focus: Compare where the two curves join and where each rounded turn sits. Review one feature at a time instead of judging the whole line as simply good or bad.

title: Seven movement families
transcription: Straight · right curve · left curve · loop · direct oval · reversed oval · capital stem
focus: Find the same named movement families in later letters. These source forms come from the Key; its original principle numbers differ from the seven-family map used in this course.

title: Parallel straight stems
focus: Compare the direction and spacing of these two straight lines. Keep your own stems light and let the hand travel across the row.

title: The right curve
transcription: Right side of an oval and the isolated right curve
focus: Follow the lower right side of the oval into its shallow finish. This curve helps you form the rounded lower turns of the i family.

title: The left curve
transcription: Left side of an oval and the isolated left curve
focus: Follow the upper left side of the oval toward the shoulder. Compare it with the right curve before making the upper turns of the n family.

title: An open extended loop
focus: Keep the long inner space open and narrow, and observe where the return path crosses the rising curve. Carry the main slant through the whole loop.

title: Three oval directions
focus: Follow the source arrows: direct begins down the left, reversed begins down the right, and inverted begins up the left. Keep the same oval axis while changing the start and direction.

title: The continuous capital stem
focus: Trace the change of curvature into the shallow oval at the foot. The Key calls this its eighth principle; it is the named capital-stem family used in this course.

title: Movement review
transcription: Straight · curves · loop · ovals · capital stem
focus: Write each named form once from the model and once from memory. Compare slant, proportion, spacing, and smoothness, then select one repair drill.
